WindDAQ Data Acquisition System

An integrated desktop platform for wind tunnel data acquisition, motion control, automated traversal testing, and probe calibration. This manual is designed for operators and covers all functional modules in detail.

1

System Overview

WindDAQ is a professional data acquisition (DAQ) desktop application designed for wind tunnel testing scenarios. It integrates device management, real-time data monitoring, motion control, automated traversal testing, probe calibration, data storage, and log management into a single unified platform for test operators.

📊

Real-time Data Acquisition

High-speed multi-channel pressure and temperature sensor data acquisition with real-time waveform display and numeric card monitoring.

⚙

Device Management

Unified management of 7 DAQ device types — SIMULATED, DAQ-P-1604, DAQ-P-1603, DAQ-P-1604Pre, DAQ-T-1603, WTN_PXI, and DSA3217 — with network scanning, online configuration, and channel editing.

➤

Motion Control

Integrated multi-axis (X/Y/Z/U) motion controllers — SIMULATED-MC, B140-MC, and WTNMC4A-MC — with jog, positioning moves, and per-axis parameter configuration.

↺

Automated Traversal Testing

Five-hole probe automated traversal with PRB/CSV interpolation algorithms, snake-scan path planning, and automatic data collection.

⚖

Probe Calibration

Total pressure, total temperature, three-hole, and five-hole probe calibration with sphere-tank gating and real-time Mach/velocity computation.

💾

Data Storage

CSV format data recording and export with customizable save paths, column selection, and real-time file writing.

System Requirements

ItemRequirement
Operating SystemWindows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit)
RuntimeWebView2 Runtime required (installer auto-detects and installs)
NetworkTCP/IP network connection to devices; ensure same subnet
Recommended Resolution1920 × 1080 or higher
2

Quick Start

For first-time users, follow these steps to get up and running:

  1. Launch the Application — Double-click the desktop shortcut or run wind-daq.exe. The application opens to the Dashboard by default.
  2. Add a Device — Click the "Manage" button above the device list to open Device Management. Click "+ New Device" to create a device profile with name, IP address, and port number.
  3. Connect the Device — In Device Management, click "Acquire" to establish a network connection and begin data acquisition.
  4. Configure Channels — Click "Edit" on the device card. In the Channels tab, configure each channel's name, engineering range, and display precision.
  5. View Data — Return to the Dashboard and switch between Chart / Card / Both / Overview view modes to monitor real-time data.
  6. Record Data — Click the "Record" button in the top toolbar to start recording data to a CSV file.
💡 Tip
If a device has been pre-configured (e.g., via auto-discovery), it will appear directly in the device list. Simply click "Acquire" to start acquisition — no manual setup needed.
3

Dashboard & Real-time Monitoring

The Dashboard is the central workspace of WindDAQ and the default view on startup. It integrates device status overview, real-time data waveforms, and numeric card monitoring.

📷 Fig 3-1: WindDAQ Dashboard — Device list, view mode switcher, Start/Record buttons

3.1 Interface Layout

The Dashboard uses a classic three-panel layout:

AreaLocationDescription
Navigation RailFar-left stripContains function entries: Dashboard, Calibration, Traversal, Logs, plus Motion (bottom), Collapse, and Settings buttons
Device List PanelLeft panelShows added devices with connection status (green dot = connected). The "Manage" button opens Device Management.
Content AreaRight main areaDisplays real-time data for the selected device. Supports Chart / Card / Both / Overview view modes.
Top ToolbarTop barWindDAQ logo & version label on the left; view-mode toggles (Chart / Card / Both / Overview) in the center; "Start" (begin acquisition) and "Record" (begin recording) buttons on the right.
Bottom Status BarBottom barShows system status (IDLE/RUNNING), device count, elapsed time, and current clock. Errors and warnings raised anywhere in the app surface here as a colored banner.

3.2 View Modes

Four view mode buttons are available at the top of the content area:

ModeDescriptionBest For
ChartReal-time waveform only — shows how each channel's data changes over timeObserving data trends and capturing transient changes
CardNumeric cards only — one card per channel showing current value, range, and mini sparklinePrecise current-value reading and multi-channel status monitoring
BothWaveform + cards in a split layoutWhen you need both trend visualization and precise numeric values
OverviewCompact grid showing all devices and their channels at a glanceQuick overview when monitoring multiple devices simultaneously

3.3 Channel Selection

In Chart or Both view, click the "Ch Select" button at the top-right of the waveform to open the channel selection dialog. By default, 6 channels are displayed.

  • Single-click a legend item: Toggle that channel's visibility
  • Double-click a legend item: Solo mode — show only that channel
  • Show All: Restore display of all channels

3.4 Zero Calibration

The "Calibrate Zero" button in the device title bar initiates a zero-point calibration. The system collects approximately 5 seconds of data and computes the zero offset.

⚠ Caution
Ensure the device is in a stable environment before calibrating zero (no wind, no pressure fluctuations). During calibration, device configuration and unit switching are locked to prevent data inconsistency.

3.5 Start Acquisition & Recording

  • "Start" button (green): Sends the start-acquisition command to the device. The device begins continuous data acquisition and pushes data to the UI.
  • "Record" button (gray/green): Starts recording acquired data to a CSV file. A file-save dialog appears to choose the save location. Click again to stop recording.
ℹ Note
"Start" controls whether the device acquires data; "Record" controls whether data is written to file. They are independent — you can Start first to monitor real-time data, then Record once the data looks stable.
4

Device Management

The Device Management module is used to add, configure, and manage all DAQ devices. Click the "Manage" button above the device list on the Dashboard to open it.

📷 Fig 4-1: Device Management — Device list, connection status, action buttons

4.1 Device Management Interface

The Device Management panel slides in from the right as a drawer and contains:

ElementDescription
"+ New Device"Create a new device profile with name, model, IP address, port, and other basic parameters
"Scan"Scan the local network for available DAQ devices
Device CardEach device shows name, model, IP:port, sample rate, channel count, and connection status
"Edit"Edit device configuration (basic info and channel parameters)
"Acquire"Connect to the device and begin data acquisition
"Disconnect"Disconnect from the device
"Delete"Delete the device profile (must disconnect first)

4.2 Editing a Device

Click "Edit" on a device card to open the device editor dialog with two tabs:

📷 Fig 4-2: Edit Device — Channels tab with batch parameter settings

Basic Info Tab

Configure the device's name, model, IP address, port number, sample rate, and other basic parameters.

Channels Tab

Configure detailed parameters for each channel:

ColumnDescription
EnabledCheck to enable the channel; uncheck to disable (disabled channels are excluded from acquisition and display)
#Channel number (01–16), fixed
Channel NameCustom name for the channel (e.g., "P1", "Patm", "T1"). Use meaningful names for clarity.
Engineering RangeThe physical measurement range (min ~ max, e.g., -5000 ~ 5000). Used for data conversion and display scaling.
PrecisionNumber of decimal places for display (e.g., 2 = two decimal places)

Batch Operations

Quick-action buttons at the top of the channel table:

  • Enable All / Disable All: One-click enable/disable for all channels
  • Reset: Reset all channels to default configuration
  • Batch apply to CH1–CH16: Set the same Range (min–max) and Precision for all channels at once
💡 Tip
After modifying channel settings, the bottom status bar shows "Configuration synced", confirming the changes are live. Click "Save" to persist, or "Cancel" to discard.
⚠ Caution
Device configuration cannot be modified during zero calibration. Wait for calibration to complete or cancel it first.

4.3 Supported Device Types

WindDAQ supports the following DAQ device models. Defaults are pre-filled when creating a new device of each type:

TypeDefault IPDefault PortDefault RateChannels
SIMULATED127.0.0.1020 Hz16 + 2 atm
DAQ-P-1604192.168.3.101900020 Hz16 + 2 atm
DAQ-P-1603(DLL managed)0100 Hz16
DAQ-P-1604Pre192.168.1.100500020 Hz16
DAQ-T-1603192.168.3.101900020 Hz16 (thermocouple)
WTN_PXI192.168.3.101900020 Hz8 (fixed names)
DSA3217192.168.1.254500020 Hz16 (with AVG/PERIOD)
ℹ Note
For DAQ-P-1603, the sample rate must be in the range 1000–500000 Hz and must also satisfy sampleRate × channelCount ≤ 250000 sps. With 16 channels the practical maximum is 15625 Hz. Out-of-range values are auto-clamped to 1000 Hz.

4.4 Network Discovery

Click "Scan" in the Device Management panel to discover DAQ devices on the local subnet:

  • The scanner broadcasts on the current PC subnet and lists responding devices with their model, IP, and MAC address.
  • Click a discovered device and then "Add" to create a profile pre-filled with the scanned IP/port — no manual entry required.
  • If a device is not found, verify it is powered on, check the IP configuration, and ensure the PC firewall allows inbound responses.
5

Motion Control

The Motion Control module controls the probe positioning system used in wind tunnel tests, supporting multi-axis (X/Y/Z/U) motion. Click the "Motion" button (with popup icon) at the bottom of the navigation rail to open a standalone motion control window.

📷 Fig 5-1: Motion Controller — Multi-axis status, JOG controls, positioning moves

5.1 Interface Layout

The motion control window is divided into two main areas:

AreaDescription
Left — Controller ListLists all configured motion controllers with name, IP address, model, and connection status. Click to switch the active controller.
Right — Axis Control PanelsCard-based display for each axis (X/Y/Z/U) with status and controls.

5.2 Axis Control Panel

Each axis card contains the following sections, top to bottom:

SectionFunction
HeaderAxis name badge (X/Y/Z/U), type label (Axis Motion Controller), and a live status indicator — Idle or Moving (with breathing animation while in motion).
Current PositionLarge-font monospace display of the current axis position (unit: mm or °), updated in real time, with a mini sparkline showing recent position history.
MonitorNegative/Positive limit indicator LEDs, "Set Zero" (set current position as zero), and per-axis "Stop" button.
JOGManual jog with "−" and "+" buttons flanking a step-size input (default 1 mm). The U axis (rotary) uses degrees (°).
PositioningTarget position input with limit validation, plus a "Move" button to execute a positioning move. The axis automatically travels to the target position at the configured speed.

5.3 Top Action Bar

  • "Connect": Connect to the selected motion controller.
  • "Disconnect": Disconnect from the controller.
  • "Stop All": Decelerate-stop all axes — the controlled stop, used for normal halts.
  • "E-Stop" (red): Emergency stop button — immediately halts all motion and locks the system. Requires manual reset before resuming operation.
🔴 Keyboard Shortcut
Press Esc at any time to trigger an emergency stop. This is the fastest way to halt motion — keep one hand near the keyboard during automated runs.

5.4 Controller Configuration

Click the "Config" tab to configure detailed controller parameters:

📷 Fig 5-2: Motion Controller Config — Communication settings and axis parameters

Communication Settings

ParameterDescription
NameController name (custom)
TypeController type (Simulated Controller / WTNMC4A / B140, etc.)
AddressController IP address
PortCommunication port number
Auto ConnectWhether to connect automatically on startup

Axis Configuration

Configure mechanical and electrical parameters for each axis:

ParameterDescription
Axis TypeLinear Axis or Rotary Axis
Step AngleStep angle in degrees (e.g., 200 = 1.8°/step)
MicrostepsMicrostepping factor for smoother motion (e.g., 8 = 8x microstep)
Lead mmLead screw lead in mm (linear displacement per revolution)
Max SpeedMaximum speed (mm/s or °/s)

Gear RatioGear ratio (rotary axis only)

🔴 Safety Warning
  • Before operating the motion controller, ensure there are no obstacles around the probe to avoid collisions.
  • When using a new controller for the first time, test the motion direction with a small JOG step first.
  • Press "E-Stop" immediately in case of any abnormality.
  • "Set Zero" sets the current position as the origin — only perform this at a known safe position.
6

Traversal Test

The Traversal Test module automates five-hole probe wind tunnel calibration. The system moves the probe to each test point according to a predefined layout, acquires pressure data, and computes flow parameters automatically.

📷 Fig 6-1: Traversal Test — Real-time data, points preview, status monitoring

6.1 Interface Layout

AreaDescription
Top Status BarTest name (Five-hole Traversal Test), current status (IDLE/RUNNING/COMPLETED), Start and Config buttons
Left PanelTarget angles (Target α/β), actual coordinates (Actual X/Y), real-time interpolation results (Alpha/Beta/Mach/Velocity/P0/Ps), and real-time pressure values (P1–P5/Patm/Tatm)
Right — Points PreviewGrid layout of all test points with color-coded progress (blue=moving, yellow=stabilizing, green=acquiring, purple=completed, gray=untested)
Bottom Status BarCSV save path, acquisition device status, positioner status

6.2 Configuring a Traversal Test

Click "Config" to open a four-step configuration wizard:

📷 Fig 6-2: Traversal Config — Step 1: Hardware (channel mapping and axis binding)

Step 1: Hardware Config

  • Unified Device: Select a single acquisition device for all probe channels, or assign devices individually per channel.
  • Start Channel: Choose the starting channel number. Click "Auto Increment Fill" to auto-fill sequential channel assignments.
  • Probe Channel Mapping: Map probe channels (P1–P5, Patm, Tatm) to specific DAQ channels (CH1–CH16) and set precision.
  • Axis Binding: Bind coordinate axes (X/Y) to motion controller physical axes and set the mapping (X axis → Alpha, Y axis → Beta).
  • Right Preview Panel: Shows live count of Points, Dwell time, and Samples.
📷 Fig 6-3: Traversal Config — Step 2: PRB/CSV interpolation algorithm and file import

Step 2: PRB/CSV Interpolation

  • PRB Mode: Choose Single PRB (one file) or Multi PRB (multiple files switched by Mach number).
  • Interpolation Algorithm: Choose Legacy (traditional PRB interpolation) or New (CSV-based interpolation).
  • Import PRB File: Import the five-hole probe calibration file (.prb format). After import, the file name, angle ranges (ALPHA/BETA), and Mach range (MACH) are displayed.

Step 3: Layout Config

Define the spatial layout of test points:

  • Pattern: Choose layout mode — line (1D sweep), rectangle (2D grid), sector (angular sweep), or custom (arbitrary point list)
  • Range & Step: Set the range and step size for each axis. The system auto-calculates the number of test points.
  • Snake Scan: Enable snake-scan path (even rows forward, odd rows reverse) to minimize travel time between points.
  • Primary Axis: Choose the primary traversal direction (X first or Y first).
📷 Fig 6-4: Traversal Config — Step 4: Configuration review and save options

Step 4: Review

Review the complete configuration summary before saving:

  • Configuration Summary: Test name, layout pattern, estimated points, interpolation algorithm, PRB file, snake scan status, primary axis direction.
  • CSV Save Path: Choose the output directory and filename. Click "Browse" to select a folder.
  • Save Options: Select which columns to include in the CSV (Point ID, Timestamp, Raw Pressure, Calculated Result). Use Select All / Deselect All for convenience.
  • Click "Save Config" to save and close the wizard.

6.3 Running a Traversal Test

  1. Precondition Check: Ensure the acquisition device is connected and acquiring, the motion controller is connected, the PRB file is imported, and the CSV save path is set.
  2. Click "Start": The system begins automated traversal. The motion controller moves the probe to the first test point.
  3. Stabilization Wait: After reaching the target position, the system waits for flow stabilization (determined by the sphere-tank gating logic).
  4. Data Acquisition: Once stable, the system automatically collects the specified number of samples and computes Alpha, Beta, Mach number, etc.
  5. Move to Next Point: After acquisition, the probe moves to the next test point and the cycle repeats.
  6. Completion: When all test points are done, the status changes to COMPLETED and the CSV file is saved automatically.

6.4 Point Status Color Legend

ColorStatusMeaning
BlueMovingThe motion controller is moving to this point
YellowStabilizingArrived at target, waiting for flow to stabilize
GreenAcquiringCurrently collecting data
PurpleCompletedThis point's test is complete
GrayUntestedNot yet tested
⚠ Caution
  • Clicking "STOP" during a test triggers a confirmation dialog. Confirming will stop the test and current progress will be lost.
  • Do not disconnect devices or close the application during a test — this may cause data inconsistency.
  • If a point fails to acquire, the system logs a warning and continues with subsequent points.
7

Calibration Modules

The Calibration module provides multiple probe calibration functions. Click "Calibration" in the navigation rail to enter. Available sub-modules include:

📈

Device Calibration

Calibrate the DAQ device itself, including zero-point and span calibration, to ensure data accuracy.

🌡

Total Pressure Probe

Total pressure probe calibration across Mach numbers, with sphere-tank gating for flow stability detection. Required channels: pProbeTotal (probe total pressure), pTunnelTotal (tunnel total pressure), pTunnelStatic (tunnel static pressure), pAtm (atmospheric pressure), tAtm (atmospheric temperature). Outputs a K-α curve and Mach/velocity per point.

🌡

Total Temperature Probe

Total temperature probe calibration with temperature recovery factor measurement and real-time CSV writing. Required channels: tTotal (probe total temperature), tStatic (static temperature), tAtm (atmospheric temperature). Outputs a recovery-coefficient vs. Mach curve.

📐

Three-hole Probe

Three-hole probe angle calibration with real-time Kb-θ/Kt-θ/Sb-θ curves and Mach/velocity computation. Required channels: p1, p2, p3 (probe pressures), pAtm, tAtm, pTotal, pStatic. Coordinate key: θ (yaw angle).

📐

Five-hole Probe

Five-hole probe angle and Mach number calibration, generating PRB/CSV calibration files for traversal tests. Required channels: p1–p5 (probe pressures), pAtm, tAtm, pTotal, pTunnelStatic, tTunnel. Coordinate keys: α (pitch) and β (yaw). Outputs Kα-Kβ, CPT-α, CPS-α coefficient surfaces.

ℹ Access Control
The probe calibration modules are access-controlled. The first time you click a calibration button, a verification dialog appears. Enter the passcode (i@windtuner) to unlock. The passcode is saved locally, so you won't need to re-enter it. A small orange lock badge appears on the navigation item when locked.

7.1 Channel Requirements Reference

Each calibration type requires a specific set of physical-quantity channels. Use the table below as a quick reference when configuring channels:

Calibration TypeRequired ChannelsCoordinate KeyOutput Curves
Total PressurepProbeTotal, pTunnelTotal, pTunnelStatic, pAtm, tAtmαK-α (single curve), Mach & velocity per point
Three-holep1, p2, p3, pAtm, tAtm, pTotal, pStaticθKβ-θ, K0-θ, Kv-θ (three curves)
Five-holep1–p5, pAtm, tAtm, pTotal, pTunnelStatic, tTunnelα, βKα-Kβ, CPT-α, CPS-α coefficient surfaces
Total TemperaturetTotal, tStatic, tAtmMachRecovery coefficient vs. Mach
⚠ Caution
All listed channels are mandatory. Missing any channel will block calibration start — the precondition check displays a red warning identifying the missing role.

7.2 General Calibration Workflow

Each calibration module uses a 3-step wizard: Basic Settings → Hardware Config → Confirm & Save.

  1. Basic Settings: Enter a calibration name (defaults to today's ISO date YYYY-MM-DD), choose a save path (required), and set the sample interval (default 50 ms, read from BatchPollIntervalMs).
  2. Hardware Config: Map each required physical-quantity channel role (e.g., pProbeTotal, pAtm) to a specific DAQ device and channel index. Bind the motion axis for the calibration sweep.
  3. Confirm & Save: Review the channel mapping and parameters, then click "Start" to launch the calibration sequence. The CSV file is created and the header row is written immediately on Start.

7.3 Sphere-Tank Gating

Some calibration modules (e.g., Total Pressure Probe) use sphere-tank gating logic to determine flow stability:

  • The system continuously monitors pressure fluctuations. When fluctuations stay below a threshold for a sustained period, flow is deemed stable.
  • Once stable, data acquisition begins automatically.
  • The timeout is configurable via TimeoutSec (default: 300 seconds).
  • If the timeout expires before stability is reached, the current point is marked as failed and the system proceeds to the next point.

7.4 Live Display

During calibration, the interface shows real-time status:

  • Top status bar: status badge, progress bar, elapsed/remaining time, target coordinate, actual coordinate, Mach number, velocity, and motion state.
  • Left data panel: P1/P2/P3 (or equivalent core channels) shown in large 20 px+ font, followed by Mach & velocity; secondary channels (pAtm, tAtm, pTotal, pStatic) are collapsible.
  • Right chart area: coefficient curves drawn on the calibration coordinate (e.g., θ for three-hole), with axis lines, tick labels, and grid lines.
💡 Tip
If a channel reading looks abnormal during calibration, pause and verify the channel mapping on the Hardware Config tab. Incorrect channel role assignment is the most common cause of bad calibration coefficients.
8

Data Storage

WindDAQ supports real-time recording of acquired data to CSV files for later analysis and archiving.

8.1 Starting a Recording

  1. Ensure the device is connected and actively acquiring (status shows RUNNING).
  2. Click the "Record" button in the top toolbar.
  3. In the file dialog, choose a save directory and enter a filename.
  4. Confirm to start recording. The button turns green to indicate active recording.
  5. Click "Record" again to stop. Data is saved automatically.

8.2 CSV File Format

Recorded CSV files contain:

  • Header row: Channel names with unit suffixes (pressure channels get _Pa, temperature channels get _degC)
  • Timestamp column: Each data row includes an acquisition timestamp
  • Data columns: One column per enabled channel, with engineering-unit converted values
💡 Tip
CSV files use UTF-8 encoding. If Excel shows garbled characters, use Data → From Text/CSV and select UTF-8 encoding in the import wizard.

8.3 Traversal Test Results

Traversal test results are automatically saved as CSV files with the following columns (based on Save Options):

  • Point ID: Test point number
  • Timestamp: Acquisition timestamp
  • Raw Pressure: Raw pressure values (P1–P5, Patm, etc.)
  • Calculated Result: Computed results (Alpha, Beta, Mach number, velocity, etc.)

Result files are saved in the user-specified directory. A hidden .traversal subdirectory stores result logs and checkpoint files for resume-from-interruption support.

9

Log Viewer

The Log Viewer displays real-time system logs for troubleshooting and monitoring. Click "Logs" in the navigation rail to open it.

9.1 Log Levels

LevelDescriptionDefault Visibility
ERRORError messages indicating operation failures or exceptionsAlways visible
WARNWarning messages about potential issuesAlways visible
INFOGeneral information (system startup, config loading, etc.)Off by default
DEBUGDebug information (high-frequency progress updates, etc.)Off by default

9.2 Log Filter Switches

Three independent filter toggles are available:

  • Hardware: Device command send/receive and hardware communication logs. On by default.
  • Info: General system information logs. Off by default.
  • Debug: High-frequency debug messages. Off by default.

Switch states are persisted in local storage and restored on next launch.

💡 Tip
WARN and ERROR logs are always visible regardless of filter settings, ensuring critical information is never missed.

9.3 Log Format

Each log entry is displayed in a compact four-column layout:

  • Time: Timestamp of the log entry
  • Level: Single-letter indicator (E=Error, W=Warn, I=Info, D=Debug)
  • Category: Source module (e.g., DEV, ACQ, MOT)
  • Message: Log content. Hardware communication logs include source info inline at the end of the message.

Settings

The Settings module configures global application parameters. Click the "Settings" gear icon at the bottom of the navigation rail.

10.1 Display Settings

Controls how data is visualized on the Dashboard:

OptionRangeDescription
ThemeLight / DarkSwitches the application color theme. Takes effect immediately.
Language中文 / EnglishInterface language toggle. Affects all labels, menus, and tooltips.
Refresh Rate1–10 HzHow often the waveform and cards refresh from the buffer. Higher values are smoother but consume more CPU. Default: 5 Hz.
Waveform Time Window10–60 secHow much historical data is visible on the chart. Buffer capacity = time window × refresh rate, clamped to a hard cap of 300 points. Default: 15 sec.
💡 Tip
If the waveform feels laggy on low-end hardware, lower the refresh rate first (try 3 Hz), then reduce the time window. Older configs using waveformBufferSize are auto-migrated to the new time-window model.

10.2 Recording Settings

Controls how data is written to CSV files during recording:

OptionDescription
Save DirectoryBase folder for recorded CSV files. The file prefix is appended to this path.
File PrefixString prepended to every recorded filename (e.g., run-001_2026-07-13.csv).
Auto-start on AcquisitionIf enabled, recording begins automatically when the device starts acquiring — no need to click "Record" manually.
Rolling Files — DurationWhen set (e.g., 600 sec), a new CSV file is created after the duration elapses. Useful for long-running tests.
Rolling Files — SizeWhen set (e.g., 100 MB), a new CSV file is created after the size limit is reached.
Auto-stop — TimeStops recording automatically after the specified total elapsed time.
Auto-stop — SizeStops recording automatically after the total recorded size reaches the limit.
Auto-stop — Record CountStops recording automatically after the specified number of files have been written (used with rolling files).

10.3 Log Configuration

  • Log Level: Choose minimum severity (Debug / Info / Warn / Error).
  • Output Toggles: Independently enable/disable Hardware, Info, and Debug log streams on the Log Viewer page.
  • Persistence: Toggle states are saved to local storage and restored on next launch.

10.4 Navigation Rail Controls

  • Expand / Collapse: Click the double-arrow button at the bottom of the rail to toggle between expanded (icon + label) and collapsed (icon only) modes. Expanded by default to help new users identify entries.
  • Settings Button: The gear icon at the bottom opens the global settings window.
  • Lock Badge: A small orange lock appears on the Calibration entry when the passcode has not been entered. Disappears after unlock.
11

FAQ

Q1: Device connection failed. What should I do?

A: Check the following in order:

  • Ensure the device is powered on and booted normally.
  • Confirm the PC and device are on the same subnet (e.g., device IP 192.168.1.x, PC IP 192.168.1.y).
  • Verify the IP address and port number are correct.
  • Try using the "Scan" function to rediscover devices.
  • Check if the firewall is blocking the connection.
Q2: Waveform shows "Waiting for data..."?

A: This means the device is connected but not yet acquiring. Click the "Start" button to begin acquisition. If no data appears after clicking, check whether the bottom status bar shows RUNNING.

Q3: Zero calibration failed or results are abnormal?

A: Before calibrating zero, ensure:

  • The device is in a stable environment (no wind, no pressure fluctuations).
  • All channels have correct engineering ranges configured.
  • No configuration changes or unit switches occur during calibration.
  • If results are abnormal, repeat the zero calibration.
Q4: Traversal test stuck at a certain state?

A: Check:

  • Is the acquisition device connected and actively acquiring?
  • Is the motion controller connected and responding?
  • Is the PRB file correctly imported?
  • Is the CSV save path valid (directory exists, write permission granted)?
  • Are there any error messages in the Log Viewer?
Q5: CSV file shows garbled text in Excel?

A: CSV files use UTF-8 encoding. In Excel, use Data → From Text/CSV and select UTF-8 in the import wizard.

Q6: Motion controller won't connect?

A: Check:

  • Is the controller powered on and booted?
  • Are the IP address and port number correct?
  • Is the network reachable (try pinging the controller IP)?
  • Is the controller type selected correctly (Simulated / WTNMC4A / B140)?
  • If first-time use, ensure axis parameters are correctly configured on the Config page.
Q7: Application fails to start or crashes?

A: Check:

  • Is the WebView2 Runtime installed? (Run MicrosoftEdgeWebView2RuntimeInstallerX64.exe from the installer directory.)
  • Check the crash log at: %APPDATA%\wind-daq\crash-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log
  • Ensure DLL files (WTNMC4A_64.dll, WTNDAQ16H_64.dll) exist in the application directory.
  • Try running the application as Administrator.

Glossary

TermFull NameDescription
DAQData AcquisitionThe process of converting physical quantities (pressure, temperature, etc.) into digital signals and recording them.
SCPIStandard Commands for Programmable InstrumentsA protocol for instrument communication.
PRBProbe Calibration FileA calibration file containing five-hole probe coefficients at various angles and Mach numbers.
Alpha (α)Angle of AttackThe angle between the airflow direction and the probe axis (pitch angle).
Beta (β)Sideslip AngleThe angle between the airflow direction and the probe axis (yaw angle).
Mach Number (Ma)Mach NumberThe ratio of flow velocity to local speed of sound, characterizing flow speed.
Total PressureTotal (Stagnation) PressureThe pressure when airflow is isentropically brought to rest.
Static PressureStatic PressureThe pressure of the airflow itself (excluding dynamic pressure component).
Atmospheric PressureAtmospheric (Barometric) PressureAmbient air pressure, used for pressure normalization calculations.
JOGJogManual incremental movement of an axis by a fixed step size.
Snake ScanSnake ScanA path planning method where even rows traverse forward and odd rows reverse, minimizing travel time.
Sphere-Tank GateSphere Tank GatingA mechanism that determines flow stability by monitoring pressure fluctuations.
Zero CalibrationZero CalibrationMeasuring and recording the zero offset with no input signal, used for subsequent data correction.
Engineering RangeEngineering RangeThe physical quantity range for a channel, used to convert raw values to engineering units.
Dwell TimeDwell TimeThe waiting period at each test point for flow stabilization.
